name: Somax Junior Soccer Ball Mastery & Fitness
description: A fun, game-based session for young players: stop-and-balance running games, dribbling slaloms, partner passing on the move, hop-and-stick landings and animal crawls.
whoItsFor: Kids aged 8-13 who play club or school soccer and want to move better and stay injury-free. A parent or coach calls the games; one ball per child.
howToRun: Use it as a second weekly session or a backyard practice; the FIFA 11+ for Kids warm-up stays the start of club training.
Keep every block playful and short - stop a drill while children still want more.
Landings: soft knees over toes, freeze for 3 s. Only 30 foot contacts of hopping in total.
No fitness testing or maximal sprints for this age; praise good technique over speed.

exercises.name: Stop-and-balance running game (freeze on one leg on 'stop')
Dribble slalom through 6 cones and back
Rob the nest (steal balls from the centre, dribble home)
Pass and move in pairs (pass, run to a new cone)
Hop and stick (land on the same leg, hold 3 s)
Single-leg balance passing with a partner
Cool-down: walk, then calf and thigh stretches

name: Somax Youth Footballer Strength Foundations
description: Teaches 12-16 year-old players the squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull and brace patterns with body weight, plus partner Nordics and short-lever Copenhagens to protect hamstrings and groin.
whoItsFor: Teenage players (about 12-16) with no gym experience. Twice a week on non-consecutive days, ideally with a coach or parent checking technique.
howToRun: Two sessions a week with at least a day between; not on match day or the day before.
Own the technique before adding reps: every rep slow down (3 s) and controlled up.
Progress one exercise at a time - e.g. Nordics 1x5 to 2x6 over 4 weeks, as in the FIFA 11+ levels.
No max lifts or testing; growth-spurt knee or heel pain means drop the jumps and see a physio.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Copenhagen plank, short lever (knee on bench)
Squat jump to stick (land and hold 2 s)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Football Fitness Starter
description: A first fitness block for adults returning to social or local-league football: jog-walk intervals, relaxed strides and a short leg-protection circuit.
whoItsFor: Adults coming back to the game (or starting it) who can walk briskly for 30 minutes but get puffed quickly on the pitch. Needs a park or oval.
howToRun: Three days a week with a rest day between; aim for 4 weeks before your first full game.
Jog at a pace you can talk at; strides are relaxed and smooth (about 70%), never all-out.
Add one jog block each week (6 to 9) before making the jogs longer.
If a hamstring or calf tightens, stop the running and do only the circuit that day.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Nordic hamstring lower (partner or anchored feet)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Off-season Tempo Runs
description: Builds the aerobic engine without hammering the legs: 12 x 150 m tempo runs at 60-70% with a walk recovery, totalling 1.8 km of quality running.
whoItsFor: Club players in the off-season who want a base before pre-season starts. Run on grass for the softer surface.
howToRun: Twice a week in the off-season, at least a day from your hardest strength day.
Tempo means 60-70% of top speed - smooth, tall and relaxed. You should be able to hold the same time every rep.
Walk 50 m back as the recovery (about 60-90 s). Week by week, cut the walk before adding reps.
Never drift into 'nearly flat out' (70-95%) - keep speed work and tempo separate.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Off-season Strength A (Lower)
description: The main off-season leg day: low box jumps, back squats, Romanian deadlifts and split squats for strength, plus Nordics, Copenhagens and calf work for hamstring, groin and Achilles resilience.
whoItsFor: Players with at least 6 months of gym experience using the off-season (and early pre-season) to get stronger.
howToRun: Pair with Strength B (upper) for 2 gym days a week, at least 48 h apart.
Weeks 1-3: squat 4x8 at about 70%; weeks 4-6: 4x5 at 80-85%; deload week 7.
Box jumps are only 15 contacts - quality, step down every rep.
Leave 1-2 reps in reserve on every set; no grinding.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Off-season Strength B (Upper & Total)
description: Second off-season gym day: trap-bar jumps for power, then bench, chin-ups, rows and push press for upper-body strength to hold off opponents, finished with hip thrusts and loaded carries.
whoItsFor: Players with gym experience who are doing Strength A on another day of the week.
howToRun: Run 48-72 h after Strength A (e.g. Monday A, Thursday B).
Trap-bar jumps: light (20-30% of your deadlift) and fast - stop the set if speed drops.
Add 2.5 kg to the main lifts when every set hits the top of the rep range.
Finish with the carries even if short on time - they train trunk and grip for shielding the ball.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Pre-season 4x4 Intervals
description: The classic 4 x 4-minute high-intensity interval, done as running or a dribbling circuit, to lift your aerobic power fast in pre-season.
whoItsFor: Players 4-8 weeks out from round 1 who already have an off-season base and want a quick, proven aerobic boost.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, never on consecutive days, and not the day after a sprint session.
Each 4 minutes at 90-95% of max heart rate - hard but even; the last minute should be the hardest to hold, not the slowest.
Jog easily for 3 minutes between efforts (about 70% max HR).
Option: do efforts 2 and 4 as a dribbling circuit around cones to add touches.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Yo-Yo Shuttle Builder
description: Trains the exact pattern of the Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test - 2 x 20 m shuttles with a 10 s jog - in sets, so your Yo-Yo score and your repeat-running in games both go up.
whoItsFor: Players who will face a Yo-Yo IR1 or beep test at club pre-season testing, or who fade late in games.
howToRun: Once a week in pre-season, 48 h from other high-intensity running.
Mark a 20 m lane and a 5 m recovery zone. Each rep = 20 m out, 20 m back, then 10 s jogging 5 m and back.
Run at about your last completed Yo-Yo level; move up half a level when all sets feel controlled.
Rest 3 minutes between sets; stop the session if you can't make the turn on time twice in a row.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Yo-Yo style shuttle (2 x 20 m + 10 s jog)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Repeat-Sprint Ability
description: Hard pre-season repeated sprints - 3 sets of 6 x 30 m, one starting every 25 s - to train recovery between high-speed efforts like a busy passage of play.
whoItsFor: Fit, experienced players in mid-to-late pre-season who already do sprint and strength work without hamstring issues.
howToRun: Once a week, never within 48 h of another max-sprint or speed-endurance session or of a match.
Full warm-up including 3 build-up runs - cold hamstrings and repeat sprints don't mix.
Each sprint is maximal; walk back and start the next on the 25 s clock. 4 minutes walking between sets.
Stop if your times drop more than about 5% from your first rep, or anything tightens.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Pre-season Strength & Power
description: Converts off-season strength into speed: hang cleans, depth jumps and heavy triples on the squat, then single-leg and groin/hamstring work and rotational med-ball throws.
whoItsFor: Strong, experienced players (squat about 1.5x body weight) in pre-season.
howToRun: Two sessions a week in pre-season, at least 48 h apart and not the day before sprint or 4x4 sessions.
Depth jumps from 30-45 cm only (no higher if you weigh over 100 kg); minimal ground contact time.
Squat triples at 85-90% with 3 minutes rest; lifts move fast or the set stops.
Total jump contacts here are 24 - well inside the advanced plyo budget.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Ball-Work Conditioning (Solo)
description: Conditioning with the ball at your feet: dribble intervals, wall-pass rounds and box-to-box carries so you build fitness and touches together when you train alone.
whoItsFor: Players training without a team (off-season, injury return late stage, or extra sessions) who have a ball, cones and a wall or rebound net.
howToRun: Use on a conditioning day, 48 h from max sprinting.
Dribble intervals: 30 s fast through a 6-cone slalom, 30 s easy juggling or toe-taps - quality touches first.
Wall rounds: 60 s two-touch passing against a wall, alternating feet, 60 s rest.
Box-to-box carries at 80% with a walk back; keep your head up every 3-4 touches.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Dribble slalom 30 s fast / 30 s easy touches
Turn-and-go: dribble, Cruyff turn, accelerate 10 m
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer In-Season Strength (MD-4)
description: One compact maintenance lift a week - few sets, heavy-ish weights - that keeps your pre-season strength and sprint speed through the season.
whoItsFor: Players with a weekend game who train 2-3 nights a week with their club.
howToRun: Once a week on MD-4 or MD-3 (Tue/Wed for a Saturday game). Research shows one session a week holds strength; one every second week does not.
Heavy but crisp: 3-6 reps at about 85% with 2-3 reps in reserve.
Only 9 jumps - in-season jump volume is about half the off-season.
Don't add new exercises mid-season - unfamiliar moves cause soreness.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer MD-2 Speed Primer
description: A short, sharp speed touch two days out from a game: drills, a few accelerations and two flying runs - enough to feel fast without fatigue.
whoItsFor: In-season players who want to stay sharp; fits before a lighter club session on MD-2.
howToRun: Only on MD-2 or earlier - never MD-1 or MD+1.
Every sprint is 95%+ with full recovery (2 minutes for starts, 4 minutes for flying runs).
Total sprint distance 120 m: low volume is the point.
Skip the flying runs if you played 90 minutes in midweek.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Match-Eve Activation (MD-1)
description: A light day-before-the-game routine: the FIFA 11+ running drills, mobility, glute and trunk switch-on and a few relaxed strides - no jumping and no max sprints.
whoItsFor: Any player the day before a match who wants to feel loose and ready rather than tired.
howToRun: MD-1 only, 15-20 minutes; this is not a fitness session.
Strides are relaxed (70-80%); no plyometrics, no maximal sprinting the day before a game.
Finish feeling better than you started.
On match day itself warm up with FIFA 11+ Parts 1 and 3.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)

name: Somax Soccer Post-Match Recovery (MD+1)
description: Easy spin, mobility and soft-tissue work the day after a game to flush the legs and check for niggles before the week's training.
whoItsFor: Players the day after a match, especially if they played most of it.
howToRun: MD+1 only: no sprints, no jumps, no heavy lifting.
Bike, swim or walk at a conversational effort.
Note any pain (hamstring, groin, ankle) - report it to your coach or physio before the next session.
Eat a proper meal and hydrate; sleep matters more than any recovery tool.

exercises.name: Legs up the wall, slow breathing

name: Somax Soccer Hamstring & Groin Protection
description: A short, evidence-led prehab block: Nordics, single-leg RDLs, Copenhagens and adductor squeezes - the two exercises that cut hamstring and groin injuries in research - plus support work.
whoItsFor: Players with a history of hamstring or groin problems, or anyone who wants the protective work in one focused session at home or after training.
howToRun: Pre-season: 2-3 times a week. In-season: once a week on MD-3 or MD-4.
Nordics: lower as slowly as you can; progress from 2x4 to 3x6 over 6-8 weeks.
Copenhagens: start short-lever (partner holds knee) and move to long-lever (ankle) when 10 reps are easy.
Expect soreness after the first two sessions - start low; stop if pain is sharp.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Single-leg Romanian deadlift (body weight or light)
Copenhagen plank, short then long lever
Adductor ball squeeze, knees bent (5 s hold)
Standing hip flexor march with band
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Women's Football Knee-Smart Strength
description: A gym session aimed at the knee: landing and lateral-bound control, single-leg strength, hamstrings, groin and calves - the qualities linked to fewer ACL injuries in female players.
whoItsFor: Women and girls (15+) playing football who want a dedicated knee-protection gym day alongside the FIFA 11+ at training.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, once a week in-season (MD-3/MD-4).
Every landing: knee over the second toe, hips back, quiet feet - film yourself from the front once a week.
Jump contacts total 39; stop jumping if knees cave and do the strength work only.
Add load to goblet squats and split squats when all sets feel 2-3 reps from failure.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Deceleration & Change of Direction
description: Learn to stop and turn well: 3-step stops, 45, 90 and 180-degree cuts and curved runs, built up from jogging to fast. Good braking is the basis of agility and protects the knee.
whoItsFor: Players of any age who are slow or wobbly changing direction, and anyone returning from a knee or ankle injury in the late stage of rehab (with physio OK).
howToRun: Once a week, early in the training week, 48 h from max sprints.
Progress each drill from 50% to 75% to 90% speed only when the stop looks controlled.
Low hips, short choppy steps into the cut, push off the outside foot, knee in line with toes.
Walk back between reps; quality drops = session ends.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Curved run around a cone arc
Mirror drill with partner or coach call
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Max-Velocity Sprint Day
description: Top-speed exposure for strong, experienced players: technical drills, wicket-style runs and flying 20-30 m sprints with long rests - the best natural protection against hamstring strains.
whoItsFor: Advanced players in the off-season or early pre-season who are hamstring-healthy and already do Nordics weekly.
howToRun: Once a week, 48-72 h from other max-sprint or repeat-sprint work.
Flying runs: 30 m build-up, then 20 or 30 m as fast as possible, relaxed face and shoulders.
Rest 5 full minutes between flying runs - this is speed, not fitness.
Total fast running is 140 m; stop early if you feel any hamstring tightness.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Speed Endurance
description: Two series of 4 x 80 m at 90-95% with 3 minutes between reps and 10 minutes between series - teaches you to hold near-top speed late in a game.
whoItsFor: Advanced players in pre-season with a solid base, regular sprint exposure and no current hamstring issues.
howToRun: Once a week in pre-season, never within 48 h of a match or another max-sprint session.
90-95%: fast and controlled, not straining. Walk back slowly between reps.
640 m of quality running in total.
Pair the following day with easy aerobic work or rest.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Home Strength (No Equipment)
description: A footballer's strength session for the lounge room: squats, lunges, single-leg bridges, push-ups, solo Nordic and short-lever Copenhagen versions, calf raises and a few pogo hops.
whoItsFor: Players who can't get to a gym or training - off-season, holidays or a busy week.
howToRun: Twice a week, 48 h apart, or once a week in-season alongside club training.
Solo Nordic: hook heels under a heavy couch, lower slowly, catch yourself with your hands.
Short-lever Copenhagen: top knee on a chair seat, lift the bottom leg to meet it.
Make it harder each week with 2 more reps or a slower 3-second lowering.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Copenhagen plank, short lever on a chair
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Goalkeeper Power & Agility
description: Keeper-specific power: lateral bounds and box jumps for take-off, explosive set-position shuffles, drop-and-rise drills, overhead med-ball throws for distribution, and shoulder care.
whoItsFor: Goalkeepers 15+ who want a power session on top of keeper coaching.
howToRun: Twice a week off/pre-season, once in-season on MD-3 or MD-4.
Jumps total 54 contacts; land softly and reset between reps.
Drop-and-rise: from set position go to ground on one side, get up and back to set as fast as possible.
Keep band shoulder work in every session - keepers load the shoulder like throwers.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: easy jog, leg swings, walking lunges, skips, side shuffles
Set position to explosive shuffle (3 m each way)
Vertical jump, catch high ball overhead
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Football Hip & Groin Mobility
description: A 20-minute floor flow for footballers' tight spots: hips, groin, hamstrings, ankles and upper back.
whoItsFor: Any player who feels stiff in the hips or groin, as a recovery-day session or after training.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week, ideally on recovery days or after training (not as a pre-game warm-up).
Move slowly and breathe; mild stretch only, never pain.
Hold static stretches 30 s; rock gently in and out on the dynamic ones.
If one side is much tighter, do an extra set on that side.

name: Somax Over-35s Football Fitness
description: A gentler fitness session for masters players: an extended warm-up, tempo runs, a few controlled strides, balance work and low-dose Nordics and Copenhagens.
whoItsFor: Players aged 35+ in masters or social leagues who want to keep playing without calf and hamstring pulls.
howToRun: Twice a week, at least 2 days apart; leave 3-4 days between any jumping or flat-out running.
Tempo runs at 60-70% with a walk back - smooth, not hard.
Calves are the masters player's weak point: never skip the calf raises.
Build up to 90-minute games over several weeks; the first game back is usually when calves go.

exercises.name: FIFA 11+ Part 1 running drills (straight, hip out/in, circling partner, shoulder contact, forwards-backwards)
Single-leg balance with ball pass (or hold)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Soccer Travel Maintenance (Hotel Room)
description: A 20-minute hotel-room session that keeps the key football qualities ticking over on tour or holiday: single-leg strength, hamstring and groin protection and a little elastic work.
whoItsFor: Players away for a week or more without a gym, or on an away trip between games.
howToRun: Twice a week while away (not the day before a game).
Hamstring walk-outs replace Nordics if you have nothing to anchor your heels.
Copenhagen short-lever on the bed edge or a chair.
Skater hops and pogos are 40 contacts - do them on carpet, not tiles.

exercises.name: Warm-up: jog on the spot, leg swings, lunges
Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on bed)

name: Somax Soccer Two-Game Week Mini-Strength
description: A 25-minute 'minimum dose' lift for weeks with two games: low-volume heavy work and the essential prehab, slotted the day after recovery.
whoItsFor: Experienced players in congested fixture periods (two matches in a week) who still want their one strength exposure.
howToRun: Do it on the day after your MD+1 recovery (MD+2), never within 48 h before a match.
Two work sets only on each lift; heavy (about 85%) but 3+ reps in reserve.
No jumps this week - the matches give enough high-intensity loading.
Drop it entirely if you are sore or played two full games.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility

name: Somax Junior Basketball Footwork & Movement
description: Game-based athletic skills for young hoopers: jump stops and stride stops, defensive slides, landing 'freezes', dribble tag and simple balance games.
whoItsFor: Kids aged 8-13 playing Aussie Hoops, school or club basketball. Needs a court or driveway, a ball each and a parent or coach.
howToRun: Twice a week, as part of practice or at home.
Teach 'quiet feet': land softly on both feet with knees over toes and freeze for 2 s.
Keep sets short and playful; finish with a game so it stays fun.
No maximal testing; total jump landings stay under 40.

exercises.name: Jog, skip, side-slide the court lines
Jump stop from a dribble (freeze 2 s)
Defensive slide, sideline to lane and back
Dribble tag (keep your ball, tag others)
Cool-down: walk, calf and thigh stretch

name: Somax Basketball Landing & Jump Foundations
description: The prerequisite for jump training: snap-downs, drop landings, squat jumps to stick, lateral hops and pogos, totalling 85 foot contacts with the emphasis on how you land.
whoItsFor: Beginner and returning players (teens and adults) before starting harder plyometrics, or anyone with knees that cave on landing.
howToRun: Twice a week, 48-72 h apart, for 4-6 weeks before moving to the advanced vertical session.
Readiness check first: 30 s single-leg stand and 30 s single-leg half squat each side.
Every landing: hips back, knees over toes, quiet - film from the front.
Stop jumping for the day if you get ankle or knee pain on landing.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Drop landing from 20-30 cm box (stick 2 s)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Off-season Lower Strength
description: The main off-season leg session for hoopers: countermovement jumps, heavy trap-bar or front-squat sets, Bulgarians and single-leg RDLs, Nordics and the tibialis/calf work that protects ankles.
whoItsFor: Players with gym experience building strength and jump height between seasons.
howToRun: Twice a week off-season (pair with Upper Strength), 48 h apart.
Main lift at 80-90% for 3-6 reps, 3 minutes rest; add load when every rep moves fast.
12 jumps at the start while fresh - jump for max height every rep.
Tibialis + calf raises every session: cheap insurance for ankles and shins.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Off-season Upper Strength
description: Upper-body strength for boxing out, finishing through contact and staying healthy: presses, chin-ups, rows, a landmine press, med-ball passes and shoulder health work.
whoItsFor: Players with gym experience doing Lower Strength on another day.
howToRun: Twice a week off-season, 48 h after the lower session.
Medicine-ball chest passes first, while fresh, as explosive as possible.
Add load when you hit the top of the rep range on every set.
Keep face pulls in - long seasons of shooting load the shoulders.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Advanced Vertical Jump
description: A full vertical-jump plyometric session for experienced jumpers: pogos, snap-downs, max countermovement jumps, game-like approach jumps, box jumps and depth jumps - 91 high-quality contacts.
whoItsFor: Experienced players who pass the landing and readiness checks (squat about 1.5x body weight, solid single-leg control) and want to jump higher in the off-season.
howToRun: Twice a week off-season, 48-72 h apart; once a week in-season and count game jumps (about 45 a game) toward your budget.
Rest 60-90 s between max-effort sets and 2-3 minutes between depth-jump sets; 5-10 s between depth jumps.
Depth-jump drop height 30-45 cm; over 100 kg, stay at the low end.
Every jump is max intent - if height drops off, stop the set.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Pre-season Court Conditioning
description: Basketball fitness on the court: sets of baseline-to-baseline sprints on short rest, defensive slide intervals and free throws while tired, to match the stop-start demands of a game.
whoItsFor: Players 3-6 weeks out from the season, after an off-season base.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, not on consecutive days, and 48 h from max sprint/jump sessions.
Sprints at about 90% with 15 s rest; 3 minutes between sets. Hold your time across the set.
Shoot 2 free throws in each set break - track your percentage under fatigue.
In-season, use this only if you are playing low minutes.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Defensive slide intervals (lane width) 20 s on / 40 s off
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Pre-season Total-Body Power
description: Turns strength into explosiveness for the season: hang cleans, trap-bar jumps, heavy squat triples, lateral box jumps and rotational throws, with single-leg and groin work.
whoItsFor: Strong, experienced players (squat about 1.5x body weight) in pre-season.
howToRun: Three lifting days a week in pre-season is the NSCA basketball model - use this for 2 of them, alternating with plyo days.
Power exercises fast and crisp; rest 2-3 minutes; stop sets when bar or jump speed drops.
Squat triples at about 85%.
Jumps here total 30 contacts - count them toward the week's budget.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball In-Season 30-Minute Lift
description: A 30-minute maintenance session to hold strength through a long season without leaving legs heavy for games.
whoItsFor: Players with 1-3 games a week who want to stay strong. Most of your time goes to court work - this is the minimum effective lift.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week, the day after recovery (GD+2) - never the day before a game.
Heavy but short: 3-5 reps at 85-90%, two or three sets, leave reps in the tank.
No jumps here - games and practice already give you plenty.
If you play big minutes twice in a week, do one session not two.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility

name: Somax Basketball Game-Eve Activation
description: A 15-minute primer for the day before a game: mobility, glute and trunk switch-on, a few relaxed court runs and your free-throw routine - no jumping or heavy legs.
whoItsFor: Any player the day before a game, or as an extra warm-up block before shoot-around.
howToRun: Game day -1 only; no plyometrics or heavy lower-body lifting.
Runs are relaxed (70%), just enough to feel quick.
Finish with 20 free throws using your exact game routine.
You should finish fresher than you started.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist

name: Somax Basketball Post-Game Recovery
description: The day after a game: easy bike or pool, ankle and hip mobility, soft-tissue work and a check for any ankle or knee niggles.
whoItsFor: Players the day after a game, especially after big minutes or back-to-backs.
howToRun: GD+1 only: no jumping, sprinting or heavy lifting.
Easy effort, nose-breathing pace.
Check your ankles: if one is swollen or painful to hop on, see a physio before playing again.
Prioritise food, fluids and sleep.

exercises.name: Foam roll calves, quads, glutes, upper back
Legs up the wall, slow breathing

name: Somax Basketball Ankle Armour
description: Balance and strength work for the most common basketball injury: single-leg balance progressions, star reaches, calf and tibialis strength, banded eversion and hop-to-stick landings.
whoItsFor: Every player, and especially anyone who has rolled an ankle before (previous sprain is the biggest risk factor for the next one).
howToRun: Three times a week for 6 weeks, then twice a week to maintain - before practice or at home.
Balance: progress eyes open, to eyes closed, to standing on a folded towel.
Hops: land and freeze 2 s without wobbling before the next one.
Painful or unstable ankle? Get it assessed before hopping.

exercises.name: Warm-up: heel and toe walks, ankle circles
Single-leg calf raise off a step

name: Somax Basketball Knee-Smart Court Warm-up
description: A 20-minute neuromuscular warm-up modelled on FIFA 11+ and Prep to Play, adapted to the court: running drills, decelerations, cuts, landings and partner Nordics.
whoItsFor: Teams and individual players (especially female players and teens) who want an ACL-focused warm-up before practice.
howToRun: Start of every practice, at least twice a week - adherence is what makes these programs work.
On game day do only the running and deceleration drills (first 8 minutes).
Knee over second toe on every stop, cut and landing.
About 30 jump contacts - count them on high-jump days.

exercises.name: Court running drills: jog, hip out/in, carioca, backpedal
Sprint to 3-step stop at the free-throw line

name: Somax Basketball Acceleration & Deceleration
description: First-step speed and braking for the court: short accelerations at full effort, deceleration to stick, lateral shuffle into sprint and lane-agility rehearsals with full recovery.
whoItsFor: Players who want a quicker first step and better defensive change of direction in the off- or pre-season.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week off/pre-season, 48 h from other max-effort sprints.
Accelerations are 98-100% with 2-3 minutes rest - total sprint distance about 100 m.
Decel: sprint 10 m then stop in 3 steps, hips low, chest over knees.
Lane agility: 3 maximal reps with 3 minutes between, timed if you can.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Sprint 10 m, decelerate to stick in 3 steps
Lateral shuffle 5 m to sprint 10 m
Drop step and sprint (react to call)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Home Strength (Bodyweight)
description: A no-equipment strength session for hoopers: split squats, single-leg bridges, push-ups, table rows, wall sits, calf raises and a little pogo work.
whoItsFor: Players without gym access (juniors, off-season at home, busy weeks).
howToRun: Twice a week, 48 h apart.
Slow 3-second lowering on every rep; add 2 reps per set each week.
Table row: lie under a sturdy table, grab the edge and pull your chest up.
Pogos: 30 contacts, quick and springy off the balls of the feet.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Aerobic Base
description: An off-season engine builder: 25 minutes of easy continuous running (or bike) plus short relaxed strides, so you recover faster between possessions.
whoItsFor: Players at any level starting their off-season, or recreational players who tire in the fourth quarter.
howToRun: Twice a week early in the off-season; swap one for a bike session if your shins or knees are sore.
Conversational pace - you should be able to speak in sentences.
Add 5 minutes each week up to 40 minutes.
Strides are relaxed (70-80%), walk back between them.

exercises.name: Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Advanced Repeat-Sprint Conditioning
description: Hard, game-like conditioning: sets of down-and-back court sprints on a 30-second clock and a sprint-slide-backpedal shell drill, for players who need to go hard for four quarters.
whoItsFor: Fit, experienced players in late pre-season with no ankle, knee or hamstring issues.
howToRun: Once a week in late pre-season only, 48 h from max-sprint and depth-jump sessions.
Each rep: baseline to far baseline and back (about 56 m); start a new rep every 30 s.
4 minutes walking and free throws between sets.
Stop if your rep time drops by more than about 5% or you start landing sloppily.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Shell drill: sprint, slide, backpedal around the key
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Mobility (Ankles, Hips, Upper Back)
description: A 20-minute mobility flow for the joints basketball stiffens: ankles (for deep landings), hips and the upper back (for shooting and rebounding reach).
whoItsFor: Players of any level on recovery days or after practice.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week on recovery days or after practice.
Move slowly; mild stretch only.
Knee-to-wall: measure the distance from toes to wall each week - more is better.
Do extra on whichever ankle or hip is tighter.

exercises.name: Deep squat hold with heels down

name: Somax Basketball Shooting Under Fatigue
description: Skill-conditioning with the ball: timed shooting rounds from five spots linked by sprints and slides, free throws at high heart rate and a game-speed finishing circuit.
whoItsFor: Players who shoot well fresh but miss late in games, training alone or with a rebounder partner.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season or as a solo off-season session.
Each round: 45 s shooting (sprint to half court and back after every make), 75 s rest. Log makes.
Two free throws immediately after each round - track the percentage.
If shot form breaks down, lengthen the rest rather than cutting rounds.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Form shooting close to the rim
5-spot shooting round (sprint to half court after each make)
Slide-and-shoot: defensive slide lane width, catch and shoot
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Low-Minutes Top-up
description: For bench players in-season: short court intervals and continuous layup work after a game or the next day, so you stay fit when you aren't getting game time.
whoItsFor: Players getting under about 10 minutes a game who feel their fitness slipping.
howToRun: Right after the game (if you played little) or GD+1 - and only if you played under about 10 minutes.
Intervals: 30 s on, 60 s off, each 'on' is 4 x 15 m sideline sprints.
Not within 48 h before your next game.
Starters skip this - use recovery instead.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Sideline sprints (4 x 15 m) 30 s on / 60 s off
Defensive slide intervals 20 s on / 40 s off
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Masters & Social Basketball Fitness
description: A gentle session for over-40s and social players: long warm-up, sit-to-stands, step-ups, balance, a few low pogos, banded rows and easy shuffle intervals.
whoItsFor: Players aged 40+ in social or masters comps who want to keep playing without calf, Achilles and ankle problems.
howToRun: Twice a week, 2-3 days apart and not the day before a game.
Leave 3-4 days between sessions with jumps; keep pogos small and springy.
Calves and Achilles: never skip the calf raises.
Shuffle intervals easy-moderate (RPE 6/10).

exercises.name: Warm-up: brisk walk, arm swings, leg swings, heel-toe walks
Side-shuffle intervals 20 s on / 40 s easy
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Bigs' Contact Strength
description: Post-play strength for centres and forwards: push press, weighted chins, landmine press, loaded carries and anti-rotation core so you hold position in the paint.
whoItsFor: Bigs and physical wings with gym experience, as an extra off-season or pre-season upper day.
howToRun: Once a week in the off- or pre-season, on a day away from heavy legs.
Carries: walk tall and slow - they train the trunk to resist being pushed.
Push press and chins in the 5-8 range, 2 minutes rest.
Med-ball passes first while fresh.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Basketball Advanced Off-season Strength
description: A heavy off-season block for experienced lifters: back squat triples, RDLs, split squats, hip thrusts, weighted chins and bench, plus Nordics.
whoItsFor: Advanced players with 2+ years of lifting who are in a dedicated strength phase (4-6 weeks) of the off-season.
howToRun: Twice a week in the off-season strength block (alternate with plyo/court days).
Squat 5 x 3 at 85-90%, 3-4 minutes rest; deload every 4th week.
Accessory work 2-3 reps from failure.
Move to the Pre-season Total-Body Power session when the off-season block ends.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Junior Basketball Strength Foundations
description: Technique-first strength for 12-16 year-olds: goblet squats, push-ups, rows, split squats, bridges, planks and landing practice.
whoItsFor: Junior players starting strength training, ideally supervised by a coach or parent.
howToRun: Twice a week on non-consecutive days.
Light dumbbell or none - technique before load; no max lifts.
Progress reps (8 to 12) before adding weight.
Growth-related knee or heel pain: drop the landings and get it checked.

exercises.name: Court warm-up: jog, carioca, defensive slides, high knees, leg swings, lunge + twist
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Junior Tennis Athlete Fundamentals
description: Movement skills for young players: split-step reaction games, side-steps and crossovers, overarm throwing and catching, hop-and-stick landings and animal crawls.
whoItsFor: Kids aged 7-13 in Tennis Hot Shots, club or school tennis. Needs a court or park, a few balls and a parent or coach.
howToRun: Twice a week, as part of a lesson or at home.
Teach technique and placement first - speed comes later.
Overarm throwing builds the serve pattern: throw with both arms, not just the playing arm.
Keep it game-like and stop while it's still fun.

exercises.name: Jog, skip, side-step the court lines
Split-step and go (react to coach's point)
Side-step / crossover step along the baseline
Cool-down: walk, shoulder and calf stretch

name: Somax Tennis Fitness Starter
description: A first fitness session for social and club players: a dynamic warm-up, short side-to-side court intervals and a simple leg, back and shoulder circuit.
whoItsFor: Adult recreational players who want to move better on court and avoid the common calf, back and shoulder niggles.
howToRun: Twice a week on non-playing days or after a hit.
Intervals are short (15 s) with long rest (45 s) - like a tennis point.
Pick weights you can lift for all reps with 2-3 in reserve.
After 6-8 weeks move on to the Off-season Strength sessions.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Side-to-side shuffle (singles sideline to centre mark)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Shoulder Care
description: A 15-minute rotator-cuff and shoulder-blade routine: external rotation strength (with slow lowering), Y-T-W raises, serratus work and internal-rotation range.
whoItsFor: Every tennis player, especially servers who feel the back of the shoulder after matches.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week, after hitting rather than before.
Slow and controlled: 3 s to lower on the eccentric external rotation.
Light band - the cuff is small; you should feel it work, never pain.
Measure internal rotation range monthly; losing range is a warning sign.

exercises.name: Band external rotation at the side

name: Somax Tennis Off-season Strength A (Legs, Trunk, Grip)
description: Lower-body and trunk strength for tennis: squats, lateral lunges, single-leg RDLs, back extensions, farmer carries and forearm work.
whoItsFor: Club and junior-competitive players (16+) with gym experience, in the off-season or early pre-season.
howToRun: Twice a week with Strength B, 48 h apart.
Squat 3-4 x 5-8 at RPE 7-8 (2-3 reps in reserve).
Lateral work matters - tennis is half sideways.
Forearm curls at the end, light, for elbow and wrist health.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Off-season Strength B (Upper & Rotation)
description: Upper-body and rotational strength: dumbbell presses, single-arm rows, cable chops and lifts, landmine rotations and cuff work for a stronger, more durable stroke.
whoItsFor: Players with gym experience doing Strength A on another day.
howToRun: Twice a week, 48 h after Strength A.
Rotation: power comes from the hips - keep the arms long and let the trunk turn.
Keep the band external rotation in every session.
Balance pushing with at least as much pulling.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Advanced Strength & Power
description: Strength-to-power for competitive players: trap-bar deadlifts, lateral bounds, split squats, rotational and overhead med-ball throws for groundstroke and serve power, and single-arm snatches.
whoItsFor: Advanced juniors (16+) and adult competitive players with solid lifting technique, in pre-season.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, 48 h apart, not the day before matches.
Throws and bounds first, maximal intent, 60-90 s rest.
Trap-bar 4 x 4 at about 85%.
Lateral bounds total 24 contacts - mostly sideways and multidirectional jumps for tennis.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Point-Play Intervals
description: On-court conditioning that matches match play: 5-20 s multidirectional 'points' with 1:3 to 1:5 work-to-rest, lateral shuffles and 90-second changeovers.
whoItsFor: Club and competitive players who fade in long sets or third sets.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week in the off- and pre-season.
Each effort is a simulated point (shadow swing at each cone), near max, then rest 3-5 times as long.
After every 2 sets take a 90 s 'changeover'.
Use a racquet and shadow swings, or have a partner feed balls if you can.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Lateral shuffle + crossover recovery 10 s on / 40 s off
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Advanced Repeated-Sprint Session
description: Repeated short sprints with incomplete recovery (efforts under 10 s at 1:4) and long ghosting patterns - for competitive players who need to recover between brutal rallies.
whoItsFor: Advanced competitive players in pre-season with good movement and no current lower-body injuries.
howToRun: Once a week in pre-season, 48 h from other max-effort sessions and not before tournaments.
Each rep under 10 s flat out, then about 4 times as long to recover (e.g. 8 s on, 32 s off).
3 minutes walking between sets.
Ghosting: move to all corners and the net shadow-hitting, 60 s continuous at match intensity.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Ghosting all corners + net (60 s on / 60 s off)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Aerobic Base
description: An easy-running engine builder for tennis: 25 minutes conversational plus relaxed strides, to recover faster between points and sets.
whoItsFor: Players of any level in the off-season, or social players who feel flat late in matches.
howToRun: Twice a week in the off-season; bike or swim instead if your knees or calves are sore.
Talk-test pace the whole way.
Add 5 minutes a week up to 40.
Strides relaxed (70-80%), walk back.

exercises.name: Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Deceleration & Recovery Footwork
description: Braking and getting back: wide-ball lateral decelerations, open-stance loading holds, crossover recovery steps and drop-step patterns - the footwork that keeps you in rallies and protects knees.
whoItsFor: Club and competitive players who over-run wide balls or are slow to recover to the middle.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week, 48 h from other max-effort sessions.
Short efforts (5-10 s) with 30-40 s rest so each rep is sharp.
Open-stance hold: sink into the outside hip, chest tall, hold 2 s before pushing back.
Add a shadow swing at each stop once the footwork is clean.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Lateral shuffle 4 m, decelerate to open stance (hold 2 s)
Drop step and sprint back for a lob
Split-step to wide ball, recover with crossover
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Serve Power & Overhead Strength
description: Power and durability for the serve and smash: overhead and slam throws, band diagonal patterns, landmine-style pressing and the cuff and scap work that protects the serving shoulder.
whoItsFor: Players wanting a bigger, safer serve in the off- or pre-season.
howToRun: Twice a week off/pre-season, not before matches.
Throws first, maximal intent, 60 s rest between sets.
Diagonal band pattern: low to high across the body, like the serve's acceleration.
Finish with eccentric cuff work every time - power needs brakes.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Pre-Match Activation
description: A 15-minute pre-match routine: dynamic warm-up, band cuff switch-on, short reactive starts and shadow swings, so you're sharp from the first point.
whoItsFor: Any player before a match or the day before a tournament starts.
howToRun: Finish about 10-20 minutes before you walk on court.
Short sprints are 5 m only - sharp but not tiring.
Keep static stretching brief before matches; save long holds for afterwards.
The day before a tournament: this plus shoulder care, nothing harder.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)

name: Somax Tennis Between-Match Recovery
description: For tournament days and the day after matches: easy movement, hip and upper-back mobility, internal-rotation range and gentle soft-tissue work.
whoItsFor: Players between matches at a tournament or the day after a long match.
howToRun: Within a few hours after a match, or the next morning.
Easy effort only - no sprints, no jumps.
Eat and drink first; recovery work comes second.
Check the shoulder and elbow: new pain means rest and a physio check.

exercises.name: Easy walk, bike or light jog
Foam roll or massage-ball forearms, calves
Legs up the wall, slow breathing

name: Somax Tennis In-Season Maintenance Strength
description: A 35-minute lift for competition season: heavy-ish trap-bar work, split squats, rows, push-ups and cuff work to hold strength without stealing energy from matches.
whoItsFor: Club and competitive players playing matches most weeks.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week early in the week, at least 2 days before a match.
Few sets, crisp reps, 2-3 reps in reserve.
No new exercises mid-season.
In a tournament week, drop to the cuff work only.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility

name: Somax Tennis Elbow & Wrist Care
description: Forearm strength and tendon care for the playing arm: slow eccentric wrist extension, flexion, forearm rotation, grip and finger-extension work.
whoItsFor: Players with a history of tennis elbow, or anyone who plays a lot and wants to keep forearms healthy.
howToRun: Three times a week on any day; takes 15 minutes.
Eccentric wrist extension: help the weight up with the other hand, lower over 3-4 s.
Start light (1-2 kg); mild discomfort that settles by the next day is OK, sharp pain is not.
Persistent elbow pain: see a physio and have your racquet and grip size checked.

exercises.name: Forearm pronation/supination with a hammer or light dumbbell

name: Somax Tennis Home Band Workout
description: A full tennis strength session with just a resistance band: squats, lateral walks, rows, chops, anti-rotation presses, cuff work and single-leg calves.
whoItsFor: Players without gym access, or anyone travelling to tournaments with a band in the bag.
howToRun: Twice a week, 48 h apart.
Choose a band that makes the last 2-3 reps hard.
Anchor the band in a door (closed and locked) for rows, chops and Pallof presses.
Progress by moving further from the anchor or doubling the band.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Masters Tennis Fitness
description: A gentle strength and movement session for players 50+: balance, sit-to-stands, step-ups, lateral steps, band rows and cuff work, with easy side-step intervals.
whoItsFor: Older social and veterans players who want to keep moving well, protect calves and shoulders, and stay on court for years.
howToRun: Twice a week on non-playing days.
Hold onto something stable for balance work at first.
Effort around 6/10 - you should finish energised, not wrecked.
Calf raises and balance work are the priorities if time is short.

exercises.name: Warm-up: march, arm circles, side steps, heel-toe walk
Side-step intervals 15 s on / 45 s off
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Tennis Mobility Flow
description: A 20-minute mobility session for tennis bodies: hips, upper back rotation, shoulder internal rotation, wrists and calves.
whoItsFor: Any player on rest days or after hitting.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week, after play or on rest days.
Long holds after play, not before - heavy stretching can blunt power.
Mild stretch only.
Spend extra time on your dominant-side shoulder internal rotation.

name: Somax Tennis Tournament Travel Session
description: A hotel-room session for tournament trips: single-leg strength, lateral work, band pulls and cuff care, done in 25 minutes.
whoItsFor: Travelling competitive players between tournaments or on rest days.
howToRun: On rest days or at least a day before your next match.
Move quickly between exercises; 30-45 s rest.
Skip the jumps on hard tiles.
If you've played 3+ matches in a row, do the mobility flow instead.

exercises.name: Warm-up: jog on the spot, arm circles, lunges with rotation

name: Somax Tennis Lower-Body Injury Prevention
description: Protects the ankles, knees, hamstrings and groin: Nordics, Copenhagens, single-leg balance and hop landings, tibialis and calf strength.
whoItsFor: Players who have had an ankle, knee or groin problem, or anyone playing several times a week.
howToRun: Twice a week, ideally after hitting or on non-match days.
Nordics: start 2 x 4, build to 3 x 6 over 6-8 weeks.
Hop landings: freeze 2 s, knee over toes.
Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain.

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Copenhagen plank, short then long lever
Single-leg calf raise off a step
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Junior Tennis Strength & Shoulder
description: Technique-first strength for 12-16 year-old players with built-in shoulder care: squats, lunges, push-ups, band rows, planks, cuff work and throwing.
whoItsFor: Junior players moving into more regular competition, ideally supervised.
howToRun: Twice a week on non-consecutive days.
Body weight and bands only at first; no max lifts.
Throw with both arms to keep the body balanced.
As they grow, add internal-rotation stretching (sleeper stretch).

exercises.name: USTA-style dynamic warm-up (jog, side shuffles, carioca, high knees, lunges with rotation)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Beginner Heavy-Bag Rounds
description: Your first heavy-bag session: five 2-minute rounds building from the jab to simple combinations, with 1-minute rests and a short core finisher.
whoItsFor: Boxing-fitness beginners who know stance and basic punches (e.g. after Shadow Boxing Starter) and have access to a bag.
howToRun: Twice a week with a rest day between.
Wrap your hands and wear bag gloves every time; stop if your wrist or knuckles hurt.
Effort 6-7/10 - technique first, power later. Breathe out on every punch.
Progress to 3-minute rounds, then to the 8-round session.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Bag round 1: jab only, move around the bag
Bag round 4: jab to the body, cross to the head
Bag round 5: free round, your best combos
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Skipping Foundations
description: Learn to skip like a boxer: technique blocks for the basic bounce, boxer step, alternate feet and high knees, built into 1-minute rounds.
whoItsFor: Anyone who trips over the rope or can't yet skip for 3 minutes; a prerequisite for most boxing sessions.
howToRun: Three times a week for 3-4 weeks.
Small jumps (2-3 cm), wrists turn the rope, elbows close to the body, land on the balls of the feet.
Rest 30-60 s between rounds; miss = restart straight away, no stopping the clock.
Graduate to the England Boxing skipping rounds once you can skip 3 minutes non-stop.

exercises.name: Warm-up: ankle bounces, calf raises, arm circles
Boxer step (shift weight foot to foot)

name: Somax 8-Round Bag Session
description: Eight 3-minute rounds on the bag, each with a theme (jab, body-head, defence-counter, power, angles, volume, combinations, flurries), 1 minute rest - the bridge between beginner rounds and a 12-round engine.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness regulars who can do 5 x 2-minute bag rounds comfortably.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week; keep at least 48 h from your hardest sprint or strength day.
Effort 7-8/10 for most rounds, 9/10 for rounds 6 and 8.
Return the hands to guard after every combination; move your feet every round.
Wraps and gloves always; stop with any hand or wrist pain.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Round 1: jab - doubles, triples, jab to body
Round 2: body-head combos (jab body, cross head)
Round 3: slip or roll, then counter 2-3 punches
Round 4: power - single shots with full rotation
Round 5: angles - pivot off after every combo
Round 6: volume - non-stop straight punches 10 s, move 20 s
Round 8: flurries - 10 s all-out every 30 s
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax 12-Round Boxing Engine
description: Twelve 3-minute rounds alternating bag, shadow and skipping, with a 10 s all-out burst every 30 s inside each bag round - heart rate near the top for most of the hour.
whoItsFor: Experienced boxers in camp or very fit boxing-fitness athletes. Heart-healthy only: bouts drive heart rate above 93-97% of max.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week in a fight camp or peak block; at least 48 h from sprints.
Bag rounds at RPE 8-9; shadow rounds sharp but controlled; skipping rounds steady.
1 minute rest between every round - stand, breathe, sip water.
Build up from the 8-round session; if form collapses after round 8, stop there.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Bag round with 10 s burst every 30 s (rounds 1, 4, 7, 10)
Skipping round - steady, last 20 s fast (rounds 3, 6, 9, 12)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Alactic Power
description: Short, maximal efforts with long rests to build explosive speed: 15 m sprints, 8-second bag flurries and rotational med-ball throws.
whoItsFor: Boxers who want faster, sharper bursts; also good for boxing-fitness athletes wanting power not just sweat.
howToRun: Once a week in the off-season and camp, 48 h from the hardest rounds day.
Everything is 98-100% - and fully recovered: 2-3 minutes between sprints, 60 s between flurries.
If speed drops, end the set; this is not conditioning.
Count it as your sprint day for the week.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Roadwork (Aerobic)
description: Classic boxer's roadwork: 30 minutes steady at a conversational pace, then relaxed tempo strides - the aerobic base behind 73% of a bout's energy.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness trainees building a base; beginners start at 20 minutes.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week, morning or on non-bag days.
Conversational pace (about 65-75% max HR).
Add 5 minutes a week up to 45.
Strides at 60-70% - smooth and relaxed.

exercises.name: Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Roadwork Round Intervals
description: Running intervals on the boxing clock: 6 x 3 minutes hard with 1 minute jogging - rounds on the road.
whoItsFor: Boxers in pre-camp or camp who already have a steady-run base.
howToRun: Once or twice a week, 48 h from the hardest bag/sparring day.
Hard = 85-90% max HR, a pace you could hold for about 15 minutes.
Jog the 1-minute 'rest' - don't stop.
Add a round every 2 weeks up to 8-10.

exercises.name: Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Strength & Power A
description: The main boxing gym day: heavy trap-bar deadlifts, landmine punch presses, rotational med-ball throws, pull-ups, plyo push-ups and neck isometrics.
whoItsFor: Boxers with gym experience in the off-season or camp.
howToRun: Twice a week (A and B) in the off-season and camp, the day after hard rounds.
Trap-bar 4 x 3-5 at 80-90%; power moves fast and fresh.
Neck isometrics: push into your hand gently, 15 s each direction - build slowly.
Final fight week: no strength work.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Strength & Core B
description: Second boxing gym day: front squats, single-arm dumbbell bench, chest-supported rows, Bulgarian split squats, carries and anti-rotation core.
whoItsFor: Boxers with gym experience doing Strength A on another day.
howToRun: 48-72 h after Strength A.
Single-arm bench trains the trunk to resist rotation - keep hips flat.
Leave 2 reps in reserve on every set.
Drop to one gym session in the second-last fight week.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Advanced Strength & Power
description: A heavy, explosive session for experienced boxers: hang power cleans, squat triples, landmine punch presses, med-ball scoop tosses, weighted pull-ups and plyo push-ups.
whoItsFor: Advanced boxers with solid lifting technique in the general-preparation phase.
howToRun: Twice a week in the off-season; drop to once a week in the second half of camp.
Cleans and squats at 85-90% for triples, 3 minutes rest.
Upper-body plyo counts toward your power budget (about half the lower-body contacts).
No strength work in fight week.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing HIIT at Home (No Bag)
description: Shadow-boxing rounds alternated with squats, push-ups and mountain climbers on a 2-minute round, 1-minute rest clock - no bag, no equipment.
whoItsFor: Beginners and busy people who want a boxing workout in the lounge room.
howToRun: Three times a week with a rest day between.
Shadow rounds: keep the guard up and the feet moving; punches snap out and back.
Bodyweight rounds: 30 s on each move, 4 moves per round.
Make it harder by moving to 3-minute rounds.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Bodyweight round: squats, push-ups, mountain climbers, plank (30 s each)
Shadow round: jab-cross-hook, slip after each
Bodyweight round: lunges, burpees, shoulder taps, squat hold
Shadow round: freestyle, 10 s fast punches every 30 s
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxer's Shoulder & Wrist Prehab
description: Keeps punching shoulders and wrists healthy: cuff and scapular band work, push-up plus, wrist and forearm strength and grip.
whoItsFor: Anyone doing regular bag or pad work, especially if shoulders ache after rounds.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week, after boxing or on rest days.
Light band and slow tempo; quality over load.
Always wrap hands for bag work - this routine doesn't replace wraps.
Wrist or knuckle pain that lasts: rest from bag work and get it checked.

exercises.name: Push-up plus (extra shoulder-blade push at the top)

name: Somax Boxing Core & Rotation
description: Trunk work for punching power and absorbing body shots: rotational and side throws, woodchops, anti-rotation presses, hanging knee raises and plank variations.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness trainees who want a stronger, more stable midsection.
howToRun: Twice a week, after rounds or on a strength day.
Throws first: rotate from the hips, explode through.
Anti-rotation work: resist the twist, breathe behind the brace.
3 x 30 s holds before adding load.

exercises.name: Warm-up: cat-cow, thoracic rotations, dead bugs

name: Somax Boxing Footwork & Agility
description: Boxer's footwork without a bag: step-drag drills, pivots, in-and-out steps, line hops and shadow footwork rounds.
whoItsFor: Beginners and intermediate boxers who feel flat-footed or off-balance when punching.
howToRun: Twice a week; good as the first part of a bag session.
Stay on the balls of your feet; never cross your feet; guard up.
Drills 20-30 s with 30 s rest so each rep is sharp.
Line hops are 40 contacts - small and quick.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Step-drag forward/back (lead foot first going forward)
Pivot off the lead foot, jab after each pivot
Shadow round: footwork only, no punches
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Fight-Camp Hard Rounds
description: The key camp conditioning day: 8 hard rounds across bag, pads and shadow with within-round bursts, then 4 x 30 s max-output bag efforts.
whoItsFor: Amateur and pro boxers in the middle weeks of a fight camp (not fight week). Pads need a coach or experienced holder.
howToRun: 1-2 times a week in weeks 3-8 of a camp; hardest day early in the week, strength the next day.
Train fight length + 1-2 rounds over the camp; this session is 8 rounds, adjust to your bout.
Monitor RPE after each round; if it's 10/10 before round 6, cut rounds rather than technique.
Hydrate between rounds - no weight cutting through training.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Bag round with 10 s burst every 30 s
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Fight-Week Sharpener
description: Taper-week session: short, crisp rounds at 70-80% and a few fast sprints - keeps speed and timing while volume drops 40-60%.
whoItsFor: Boxers in the final week before a bout.
howToRun: Fight week: 2 sessions early in the week, then just shadow and mobility.
Keep intensity (snap and speed), cut the volume; you should leave feeling fresh.
No strength work and no new drills this week.
Don't use training to make weight - that's a separate, supervised plan.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles

name: Somax Boxing Recovery & Mobility
description: A recovery session after hard rounds: easy cardio, then mobility for the punching chain - hips, upper back, shoulders, chest, wrists and neck.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness trainees the day after hard sessions.
howToRun: The day after your hardest rounds or sparring-free conditioning day.
Easy effort only.
Gentle neck range of motion - never force it.
Any concussion symptoms (headache, dizziness, fogginess): no training until medically cleared.

exercises.name: Easy bike, walk or light skipping
Gentle neck range of motion (nod, turn, tilt)

name: Somax Over-40s Boxing Fitness
description: Boxing fitness for older beginners: a longer warm-up, six 2-minute rounds at a steady effort, balance work and a little strength.
whoItsFor: Adults 40+ (including those new to exercise with medical clearance) who want the fun of boxing without high-intensity overload.
howToRun: Twice a week, 2-3 days apart.
Rounds at 6-7/10 - you can talk in short sentences between rounds.
Get a medical check first if you have heart, blood pressure or joint concerns.
Shadow box instead of the bag if your wrists or shoulders complain.

exercises.name: Warm-up: march, arm circles, hip circles, step-touch
Bag or shadow round: jab-cross at a steady pace
Bag or shadow round: hooks and uppercuts, slow and controlled
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Travel Shadow Session
description: A 20-minute hotel-room session: shadow rounds with technical themes and short bodyweight bursts on the rest minute.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness regulars away from their gym.
howToRun: Twice a week while away.
3-minute rounds; on the 'rest' minute do 20 s of the listed exercise, then 40 s rest.
Visualise an opponent - defence and feints in every round.
Quiet, low-impact options are fine (squats instead of jumps).

exercises.name: Warm-up: shadow at 50%, arm and hip circles
Shadow round: jab work and footwork
Shadow round: fast hands - 10 s bursts every 30 s

name: Somax Partner Pad-Work Conditioning
description: Partner pad rounds that swap holder and hitter each round: combinations, defence on the pads' return shots and burnout rounds.
whoItsFor: Pairs at a boxing-fitness class or training buddies; the holder needs basic pad-holding skills.
howToRun: Twice a week; swap roles every round so each person hits 4 rounds.
Holder calls combinations and meets the punch - don't push the pad into the punch.
Hitter returns hands to guard after every combo; defend the holder's slow return swings.
Wraps and gloves on; stop with any wrist pain.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Pad round: combo then slip or roll the holder's return
Pad burnout: straight punches 20 s on / 10 s off
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Boxing Upper-Body Endurance (Home)
description: Shoulder and arm endurance for keeping your hands up: push-up variations, band punches, shoulder taps, guard holds and plank-to-push-ups in timed rounds.
whoItsFor: Boxers whose hands drop late in rounds, training at home.
howToRun: Twice a week, not the day before hard rounds.
Rounds of 40 s work / 20 s rest through the list, 3 times.
Band punches: anchor behind you, punch straight with full extension, control the return.
Guard hold: hands at cheekbones, elbows in, light dumbbells or none.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping + shoulder, hip and ankle circles
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Junior Boxing Fitness (Non-Contact)
description: Non-contact boxing fitness for 10-15 year-olds: skipping games, shadow technique rounds, footwork drills and bodyweight strength - no sparring, no head contact.
whoItsFor: Junior boxers and kids in boxing-fitness programs, supervised by a coach or parent.
howToRun: Twice a week with at least a day between.
Rounds are 1.5-2 minutes for this age with 1 minute rest.
Technique before speed; praise good guard and footwork.
This app covers conditioning only - head contact and sparring need a registered club and coach.

exercises.name: Skipping games (bounce, boxer step, high knees)
Shadow round: jab-cross with step forward and back

name: Somax AFL Match-Eve Activation (MD-1)
description: The optional 10-15 minute primer for the day before a game: mobility, glute and trunk switch-on, a few relaxed run-throughs and light kicking and handballing - no jumps, no max sprints.
whoItsFor: Footballers the day before a Saturday game (Friday) who like to move rather than rest completely.
howToRun: MD-1 only, 10-15 minutes, or rest completely - both are fine.
Run-throughs at 70% only; at least 48 h between max sprint or plyometric efforts and the game.
No alcohol in the 48 h before a game.
On match day, warm up with Prep to Play or FootyFirst warm-up drills.

exercises.name: Light kicking and handball, both sides

name: Somax AFL Off-season Home Strength
description: A no-gym off-season strength session for footballers: split squats, single-leg RDLs, push-ups, rows, partner Nordics, Copenhagens and calf work.
whoItsFor: Community players without gym access over the summer break, or as a base before pre-season.
howToRun: Twice a week through the off-season, 48 h apart.
Slow 3-second lowering; add 2 reps per set each week.
Nordics: follow the FootyFirst progression (1 x 6, then 2 x 5, then 2 x 8).
Partner not available? Hook your heels under a couch.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Off-season Size & Strength (Gym)
description: A full-body off-season hypertrophy session (3-4 sets of 8-12) to add muscle and robustness before pre-season strength and power work.
whoItsFor: Players with gym experience, especially younger or lighter players wanting to add size for contact.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week across a 4-6 week off-season block, 48 h apart.
Loads around 65-75% (2-3 reps in reserve); rest 90 s.
Keep Nordics and Copenhagens in even in a size block.
Eat enough protein (about 1.6 g/kg/day) or the size won't come.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Off-season Low-Impact Aerobic
description: Aerobic base without the pounding: steady bike or rower plus short surges, so you start pre-season fit without sore shins or Achilles.
whoItsFor: Players coming off a long season with leg niggles, heavier players, or anyone in the first 2-4 weeks back.
howToRun: Twice a week in the first half of the off-season, alongside one easy run.
Steady parts conversational (about 70% max HR); surges hard but short.
Swap freely between bike, rower, ski erg or swimming.
Build to running-based sessions 4 weeks before pre-season starts.

exercises.name: Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Ruck & Key-Position Contest Power
description: Power for marking and ruck contests: approach jumps, single-leg take-offs, depth jumps, heavy trap-bar triples, pull-ups and med-ball throws.
whoItsFor: Ruckmen and key-position players with a strong training history, in the off- or pre-season.
howToRun: Twice a week off/pre-season, 48-72 h apart; once a week in-season with the jump work halved.
Jumps total 48 contacts - all max intent with full recovery.
Depth jumps from 30-45 cm only (lowest end over 100 kg).
Single-leg take-offs: train both legs, more reps on your weaker side.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Midfielder Repeat-Effort Conditioning
description: Repeat-effort work for on-ballers: sprint, get down to the ground and up, sprint again - in sets on a 30 s clock, mimicking stoppage-to-stoppage running.
whoItsFor: Midfielders and high half-forwards/backs in late pre-season with good running base and no hamstring issues.
howToRun: Once a week in late pre-season, 48 h from max-sprint and from games.
Each rep: 20 m sprint, chest to ground, up, 20 m sprint the other way (pick up a ball on the second run).
Start a new rep every 30 s; 4 minutes walking between sets.
Stop if rep quality or speed clearly drops.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Repeat effort: 20 m sprint - ground - up - 20 m sprint (every 30 s)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Masters Footy Fitness
description: A gentler session for masters footballers: an extended FootyFirst-style warm-up, tempo running, a few kicks on the run, balance and low-dose hamstring, groin and calf work.
whoItsFor: Players 35+ in masters or community reserves who want to keep playing without calf and hamstring strains.
howToRun: Twice a week, 2-3 days apart; leave 3-4 days between any flat-out running or jumps.
Tempo runs at 60-70% with a walk back.
Never skip the calf raises - calves are the masters player's weak link.
Build up minutes in games gradually after any break.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Kick on the run to a target (both feet)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Kick-Run Skill Conditioning
description: Fitness and skill together: kick-and-run loops, ground-ball pick-ups, handball under fatigue and short sprints to a lead, in 4-minute blocks.
whoItsFor: Players (pairs or small groups) in pre-season or the off-season who want conditioning that keeps their foot skills sharp when tired.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, 48 h from max-sprint days.
Each block 4 minutes continuous at a hard but sustainable pace, 2 minutes easy between.
Count clean disposals; quality kicks matter more than distance covered.
Use both feet and both hands in every block.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Block 1: kick 30 m to partner, run 40 m to a new cone, repeat
Block 2: ground-ball pick-up, handball, sprint 15 m lead, mark
Block 4: lead 20 m, mark, turn, kick to 30 m target
Easy jog and handball between blocks
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Shoulder & Contact Prehab
description: Shoulder and neck robustness for tackling, bumping and falling: cuff and scapular band work, push-up plus, neck isometrics, wheelbarrow holds and safe falling practice.
whoItsFor: Any footballer, especially after a shoulder injury (with physio clearance) or players new to contact.
howToRun: Twice a week through pre-season and in-season.
Light band, slow tempo.
Neck isometrics: gentle pressure only, 10-15 s each direction.
Concussion: no contact training until day 21 and medically cleared.

exercises.name: Falling and rolling practice (both shoulders, from kneeling)

name: Somax AFL 20-Minute In-Season Top-up
description: The minimum effective prehab and strength for a busy in-season week: Nordics, Copenhagens, single-leg strength and a few pogo hops in 20 minutes.
whoItsFor: Community players who can only make one club night some weeks.
howToRun: Once a week on MD-4 or MD-3 when you can't get to the gym.
Nordics and Copenhagens weekly are the priority in-season.
Pogos are only 30 contacts - in-season jump volume stays low.
Never on MD-1.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)

name: Somax AFLW Gym Strength
description: A gym session for women's footy built around the knee and contact: landing control, squats, single-leg strength, hamstrings, groin, upper-body pushing and pulling.
whoItsFor: AFLW and community women's players (15+) who want a structured gym day alongside Prep to Play.
howToRun: Twice a week in pre-season, once a week in-season (MD-4/MD-3).
Pair with Prep to Play warm-ups at every training - ACL risk is much higher in women's footy.
Landings: knee over second toe, quiet feet; jumps total 33 contacts.
Add load when you reach the top of the rep range with 2 reps in reserve.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike or rower easy, then hip and shoulder mobility
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax Junior Footy Strength Foundations
description: Technique-first body-weight strength for 12-16 year-old footballers: squat, lunge, push, pull, brace, partner Nordics and landing practice.
whoItsFor: Junior footballers starting strength work, supervised by a coach or parent.
howToRun: Twice a week, not on game day or the day before.
No max lifts; quality reps with a slow lowering.
Juniors: ideally no more than 2 games a week and 25 a season (AFL Junior Rules).
Growth-spurt knee or heel pain: drop the landings and see a physio.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)

name: Somax AFL Max-Velocity Speed Day
description: Top-speed exposure for experienced footballers: running drills, wicket runs and flying 20-30 m sprints with long rests - regular max-speed running is one of the best hamstring protectors.
whoItsFor: Advanced players in the off-season and pre-season who are hamstring-healthy and doing Nordics weekly.
howToRun: Once a week, 48-72 h from other max-sprint or repeat-sprint work and from games.
Flying runs: 30 m build-up, then 20-30 m as fast as possible, relaxed.
5 minutes rest between flying runs; total fast running 140 m.
In-season, keep 2-3 flying runs on MD-4 to hold top speed.

exercises.name: FootyFirst-style warm-up (jog, side-to-side, carioca, butt kicks, leg swings, lunges)
A-skips, B-skips, straight-leg bounds (Rob Jackson T1-style drills)
Cool-down: walk and stretch (hips, hamstrings, calves, chest)
